title: MIT researchers track AI chatbot responses to 2026 U.S. midterm election queries
excerpt: The LLM Election Observatory monitors how AI systems respond to election-related questions over time.
bodyHtml:
MIT researchers have built a dashboard called the LLM Election Observatory to examine how popular artificial intelligence chatbots respond to questions about the 2026 U.S. midterm elections. The team, led by Professor Adam Berinsky, Assistant Professor Chara Podimata, and Professor Charles Stewart III, tracks how different AI systems respond to a fixed set of questions on topics including election certification, result predictions, and news coverage.

The team runs these questions through the chatbots every few days to monitor how responses vary based on user location, political party affiliation, and identity. The researchers intend to document how these information environments evolve as the election approaches. The dashboard presents the underlying data and preliminary descriptive analyses, and the team plans to make the dataset available for other researchers to study.

The researchers have not yet completed a full longitudinal analysis of the data. While broad patterns are visible in the 2026 data, the team cannot yet determine how stable those differences are or how they move over the course of the election. The team expects the dashboard to evolve as the data and methods evolve.
